_comment: Deny rules for the unattended Claude step in spec-pipeline.yml.
--allowedTools is a grant, not a limit: what it leaves out is not forbidden,
it merely has nothing pre-approving it. A command file's allowed-tools is a
grant too, and it applies even in a -p run in a folder nobody has trusted.
Deny is the only one of the three that is a limit. It is evaluated first and
nothing overrides it -- not --allowedTools, not a skill's allowed-tools, not a
PreToolUse hook returning allow. That is why the reduction this job wants is
written here as well as taken away there: if someone later re-adds a broad
grant to a command file, these rules still hold.
Every rule here is one that no ! preprocessing line in /spec, /plan or
/acceptance can match. That matters: a preprocessing command matching a deny
rule aborts the whole invocation, and that abort is silent -- exit 0,
is_error false, an empty result. Broad rules like Bash(cat *) or
Bash(python3 *) would break these commands rather than confine them, so the
rules below name the dangerous forms instead: arbitrary code, network egress,
the environment, and the credential paths.
